blocks.value: An identifier is the name you give to a program component: a class, object, or variable. Java has rules for what counts as a valid identifier:

- Must begin with a letter, an underscore (_), or a dollar sign ($). It cannot begin with a digit.
- Can contain any combination of letters, digits, underscores, or dollar signs. No spaces are allowed.
- Cannot be a reserved keyword.
- Is case-sensitive: number, Number, and NUMBER are three different identifiers.
- Cannot be true, false, or null. These are reserved values, not keywords, but still off-limits.

By convention, class names should start with a capital letter.
Reserved words (keywords) have special meaning to the Java compiler and can never be used as identifiers. Here are all of them:

abstract   continue   for          new        switch
assert     default    goto         package    synchronized
boolean    do         if           private    this
break      double     implements   protected  throw
byte       else       import       public     throws
case       enum       instanceof   return     transient
catch      extends    int          short      try
char       final      interface    static     void
class      finally    long         strictfp   volatile
const      float      native       super      while
